# OCFS1 format references and fixture

The production reader is original AGPL-3.0-only Rust. Oracle's September 2003 archive contains `branches/ocfs-1.0/tools/sizetest/disk.txt` from r8, listing the precise field positions and widths for the release 1 disk records. The same revision's `debugocfs` changes show directory slot addressing and continuation traversal. The September 2004 commits confirm how file entries refer to their containing directory sector and how the driver handles validity and deletion flags. [September 2003 archive](https://oss.oracle.com/pipermail/ocfs-commits/2003-September.txt.gz) · [September 2004 archive](https://oss.oracle.com/pipermail/ocfs-commits/2004-September.txt.gz)

Oracle's December 2003 archive preserves the transitional source that still used the release 1 disk version. Old `ocfs.h`, `alloc.c`, `dir.c` and `namei.c` provide the constants and behavior for the OracleCFS 1.2 records. The February 2004 archive records the disk version change from 1.2 to 2.0. The mainline Linux OCFS2 source documents the compatibility prefix. [December 2003 archive](https://oss.oracle.com/pipermail/ocfs2-commits/2003-December.txt.gz) · [February 2004 archive](https://oss.oracle.com/pipermail/ocfs2-commits/2004-February.txt.gz) · [Linux compatibility header](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.12/fs/ocfs2/ocfs1_fs_compat.h)

`tests/fixtures/make-fixture.py` independently writes an invented 4 MiB image with a directory continuation, a nested directory, direct and external extent records, and a deleted entry. Its zlib SHA-256 is `16634828d9c3db811bc4da4257fcfebad7076d45c1da0158d4fe3c23770bcf88`. The tests use Oracle's archived layouts as the reference for field placement. The fixture was generated from those records and contains invented contents. A native `mkfs.ocfs` or FSCat export has yet to be compared byte for byte.
